newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras Central Bank sees 4.5 pct growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Honduras Central Bank sees 4.5 pct growth in 1997.

text.p: Honduras could hit economic growth of 4.5 percent in 1997, reduce inflation to about 16 percent and reverse years of trade deficits, Central Bank vice president Daniel Figueroa said on Friday.
"The monetary program's goals are reachable and consistent with the country's economic conditions." he told a media conference.
The country's economy grew three percent in 1996, inflation was 24.9 percent and the trade deficit was almost $400 million.
The fiscal deficit compared with gross domestic product should remain at three percent for the year, the same as in 1996, Figueroa said.
In 1997, the central bank planned to place 1.7 billion lempiras ($133 million) in the banking system to control the currency's depreciation and inflation.
Figueroa estimated coffee sales and expanding banana exports should reverse the trade deficit and allow the country to break even, or post a surplus for the first time in more than two decades.
